chapter: Annex, Cadillac and the Ory-Oliver band
title: Leading his own band at the Annex and Cadillac cabarets
summary: He names the piano, violin, drums and entertainers he hired at the Annex, how it ended when he fell ill, and his later band at the Cadillac.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Arlington Annex. I think you're right, Charles. So, I hired my band. Myself. I was playing piano. I hired P. Buckeyes to play violin. My drummer was Chris Minor. And I had three entertainers. That was Willie Jackson. Gets acquainted with Willie Jackson, when I was playing with Jack Carey's Orchestra, at the Come Clean Hall, because he lived in Gretton then. And he always asked me, he says, at times if you get a job for me to sing, I'd like to have a job to sing, because he was a songwriter. Well, I remember that. And I kept him in view. When he opened up, I hired Willie. He had moved from Gretton on this side, on St. Andrews Street. He hired him, or hired a fellow called Noogie Johnson. Noogie. And I had another one they called Arthur Wynn. Three entertainers. And they sang and danced right on the bandstand. And we waste that job, waste that job there about over two years. I got sick. I had to leave the job. I goes down to get Paul Dominguez to play a violin in my place. Well, a little drum player, he says, well, I mean, I gets Freddie Washington. Right there. Then I goes down to get Paul Dominguez. My drum player by me quit, and Chris Minor, he quits. Well, Paul Dominguez, he gets Louis Contrell to play a drum. They plays the job, you know, ran out, closed. Then I goes down, plays over Conti, Ramport, they call it Cadillac.
Conti and Ramport. Ramport. Called the Cadillac.
Which corner? Do you remember? Is it on the riverside or? No, it was on the uptown side. Uptown? Yeah. Near the river or towards the lake? Yeah, the river.
Towards the river, up the lake. Yeah, the river.
Towards the river, up the lake.

It's a vacant lot there now. Well, I had on that job, I played the piano for that job. I had Albin Nicholas. I'm crying there. And I had a banjo player, they called Joe Robinson. He sang and played a banjo. Very fine songs. He was Nookie Johnson's brother. And on drums, I had Arnold Dupes. And I left the job. And I left the job. Yeah, on trumpet, I want to say it too. Had Anorma Twier. And I left the job. Yeah, on trumpet, I want to say it too. Had Anorma Twier. That was a Cadillac job. He was with you later at the Tuxedo. That's the time of the Tuxedo. Yeah. Well, I was a cabaret.
That was a cabaret. That was a cabaret. That was a cabaret. Well, I went out. I was out to field then.
